sections.title: Overview
descriptions: Quinn Jay Adamson is an American Fork police lieutenant. This page includes his employment and compensation records and covers his involvement in two encounters documented on this site: the Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben) case and the arrest of Cody Greenland.

His role in the Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben) case included removing a sign, helping seize Sheldon Norcross’s phone and arrest him, and coordinating the March 11 Airbnb operation and detainee transport.

sections.title: Employment
descriptions: Officer Quinn Jay Adamson began working for the American Fork Police Department on June 8, 2010. He was employed by the Provo City Constable’s Office from September 29, 2017, through October 11, 2018.

contents.text_value: March 11, 2026, afternoon: Adamson contacted the property owner about the sign, removed it after she withdrew permission, and gave it to Richardson as evidence. He helped seize Sheldon Norcross’s phone and moved his arm into a cuffing position while Richardson applied the handcuffs. Adamson’s report records Sheldon saying he was trying to lock the phone; Nicosia’s interview records Sheldon saying he pressed the power button to black out the screen, not delete anything. See pages 14–16 and 18. Adamson wrote a supplement describing the March 11 sign and phone encounter, his surveillance of the Airbnb, and serving the homeowner with the warrant. The recording places Sheldon’s arrest at about 3:23 p.m., before the evening Airbnb operation.

At the October 14, 2026 lawsuit press conference, plaintiffs’ attorney Solomon Radner alleged that Lieutenant Quinn Adamson cut down and seized the GoFundMe sign from a neighbor’s fence on March 11. Radner said the neighbor initially permitted the sign and alleged that police pressured her to withdraw that permission before removing it. This is the plaintiffs’ attorney’s allegation, not a court finding.

contents.label: Solomon Radner’s sign-removal allegation — October 14 press conference (20:40–21:25; Adamson named at 20:52)

contents.text_value: March 11, 2026, evening: Adamson’s supplement says he surveyed the Airbnb location before the operation and later served the homeowner with a copy of the warrant. Richardson assigned him to the perimeter. His recorded calls and texts also show him updating Chief Paul and Sgt. Stowers about the operation and coordinating with detectives and directing officers to transport the detainees to AFPD and keep them in separate holding cells for questioning. See pages 11 and 16 and the linked recording analysis.

Adamson was among the officers involved in Greenland’s April 17, 2020 arrest. Greenland’s federal lawsuit alleged that Adamson used a Taser on him multiple times without warning and failed to stop another officer’s use of force. Adamson was named as a defendant. The lawsuit was later settled and dismissed with prejudice; the settlement did not establish that the allegations were proven.
